title: Bash
label: Bash
desc: The Bourne Again Shell: interactive command line and scripting language.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Check the shell, its version and how a script starts.

snippets.code:
# Check which Bash is in use and its version
bash --version | head -n 1
echo "$BASH_VERSION"

# Start a login shell or a plain interactive subshell
bash -l
bash --norc --noprofile

# Run one command without loading startup files
bash --noprofile --norc -c 'echo "$BASH_VERSION"'

# Save this as hello.sh, then run it
chmod +x hello.sh
./hello.sh

# Or run it without the execute bit
bash hello.sh

# The shebang chooses the interpreter
head -n 1 hello.sh   # #!/usr/bin/env bash

sections.title: Basic Syntax
sections.description: Comments, statements and the shebang line.

snippets.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Comments start with a hash and run to the end of the line
echo "Hello, world"      # trailing comment

# Statements are separated by newlines or semicolons
name="Ada"; echo "Hello, $name"

# A trailing backslash continues the command on the next line
printf '%s\n' \
  "first line" \
  "second line"

# Braces group commands in the current shell
{ echo "one"; echo "two"; } > out.txt
cat out.txt

# Parentheses group commands in a subshell
( cd /tmp && pwd )
pwd   # still the original directory

sections.title: Variables
sections.description: Assign values and use the special variables Bash provides.

snippets.code:
# Assignment: no spaces around the equals sign
name="Grace"
age=36
readonly project="cheatrs"

# Use a variable with $name or ${name}
echo "$name is $age years old"

# Local variables inside functions need the local keyword
greet() {
  local greeting="Hello"
  echo "$greeting, $1"
}

# Read-only variables reject later assignments
# project="other"   # error: project: readonly variable

# Positional and script variables
echo "script: $0"        # name of the script
echo "arguments: $#"     # how many were passed
echo "all: $@"           # every argument, quoted separately
echo "status: $?"        # exit status of the last command
echo "pid: $$"           # process id of the current shell
echo "line: $LINENO"     # current line number

sections.title: Quoting and Escaping
sections.description: Pick quotes that expand, preserve or escape text.

snippets.code:
# Double quotes expand variables and command substitution
name="Ada"
echo "Hello, $name"        # Hello, Ada
echo "Today is $(date +%F)"

# Single quotes keep every character literal
echo 'Cost: $100'          # Cost: $100

# Backslash escapes a single character
echo "She said \"hi\""     # She said "hi"
echo 'It'\''s fine'        # It's fine

# $'...' interprets escapes like \n and \t
printf '%s' $'line one\nline two\n'
printf 'tab\tseparated\n'

# Quote expansions to keep spaces intact
printf '[%s]\n' "  padded  "

# An unquoted variable is split into words
items="red green blue"
for item in $items; do echo "$item"; done

sections.title: Parameter Expansion
sections.description: Edit and test values without spawning extra commands.

sections.title: Conditionals
sections.description: Branch with arithmetic, string and file tests.

snippets.code:
# if / elif / else with arithmetic tests
count=12

if (( count > 10 )); then
  echo "more than ten"
elif (( count == 10 )); then
  echo "exactly ten"
else
  echo "fewer than ten"
fi

# String and file tests
name="Ada"
if [[ -n $name && -f /etc/hostname ]]; then
  echo "$name has a hostname file"
fi

# One-line form
[[ -d /tmp ]] && echo "/tmp is a directory"

sections.title: Loops
sections.description: Repeat work over lists, ranges and input.

snippets.code:
# for over an explicit list
for fruit in apple banana cherry; do
  echo "fruit: $fruit"
done

# C-style arithmetic loop
for ((i = 1; i <= 3; i++)); do
  echo "round $i"
done

# while with a counter
count=3
while (( count > 0 )); do
  echo "countdown $count"
  ((count--))
done

# Read input line by line
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' | while IFS= read -r line; do
  printf 'line: %s\n' "$line"
done

# until runs while the condition is false
n=0
until (( n == 2 )); do
  echo "n=$n"
  ((n++))
done

sections.title: Functions
sections.description: Wrap commands, pass arguments and return status.

snippets.code:
# Capture stdout instead of printing it
square() {
  local n="$1"
  printf '%s\n' "$(( n * n ))"
}

result=$(square 7)
echo "7 squared is $result"   # 49

sections.title: Arrays
sections.description: Store ordered lists and key-value pairs.

snippets.code:
# Indexed array
fruits=("apple" "banana" "cherry")
echo "${fruits[0]}"      # apple
echo "${fruits[@]}"      # all elements
echo "${#fruits[@]}"     # 3
fruits+=("date")         # append
unset 'fruits[1]'        # remove one element

# Loop over every remaining element
for fruit in "${fruits[@]}"; do
  echo "$fruit"
done

# Associative arrays require declare -A
declare -A ports=(
  [http]=80
  [https]=443
  [ssh]=22
)

echo "${ports[https]}"   # 443
for key in "${!ports[@]}"; do
  echo "$key -> ${ports[$key]}"
done

# Slices keep a range of an indexed array
numbers=(10 20 30 40 50)
echo "${numbers[@]:1:2}"   # 20 30

sections.title: Reading Input
sections.description: Ask the user for values and parse options.

snippets.code:
# Prompt and read a line
read -r -p "Your name: " name
echo "Hello, $name"

# Silent input for passwords
read -r -s -p "Password: " secret
echo
echo "read ${#secret} characters"

# Read with a timeout and a default answer
read -r -t 5 -p "Continue? [y/N] " answer
answer=${answer:-n}
echo "choice: $answer"

sections.title: Output and Echo
sections.description: Print readable text, formatted values and colour.

snippets.code:
# echo adds a newline; printf gives control over format
echo "plain text"
printf '%s\n' "formatted text"
printf 'name=%-8s score=%03d\n' "Ada" 97

# Write to stderr
echo "warning: disk almost full" >&2

# Keep escapes literal unless -e is used
echo -e "first\nsecond"

# ANSI colours: reset with \033[0m
green='\033[0;32m'
red='\033[0;31m'
reset='\033[0m'

printf "${green}ok${reset}: build finished\n"
printf "${red}fail${reset}: 2 tests failed\n"

# Only use colour when stdout is a terminal
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
  echo "interactive terminal"
fi

sections.title: Redirection
sections.description: Route stdout, stderr and extra descriptors.

snippets.code:
# stdout, stderr and both
ls /etc > listing.txt          # stdout only
ls /missing 2> errors.txt      # stderr only
command > all.log 2>&1         # both to the same file

# Append instead of truncating
echo "new run" >> all.log

# Discard output
command > /dev/null 2>&1

# Here-document with variable expansion
cat <<EOF
user: $USER
home: $HOME
EOF

# Open a file on descriptor 3
exec 3> log.txt
echo "first line" >&3
echo "second line" >&3
exec 3>&-

# Feed one line through a pipe instead of a temporary file
printf 'one two three\n' | wc -w   # 3

sections.title: Pipes and Filters
sections.description: Connect commands and filter the stream in flight.

snippets.code:
# Count files and show the first sorted names
ls /etc | wc -l
printf '%s\n' cherry apple banana | sort | head -n 2

# Keep stderr out of the pipe
grep -r "PermitRootLogin" /etc/ssh 2>/dev/null | head -n 5

# pipefail makes a failing stage fail the whole pipeline
set -o pipefail
false | true
echo "status: $?"

# tee writes to a file and keeps the stream flowing
printf 'alpha
beta
' | tee words.txt | wc -l

# xargs turns lines into arguments
printf 'a.txt
b.txt
' | xargs -n 1 echo "file:"

# Process substitution compares two sorted streams
diff <(printf 'b
a
' | sort) <(printf 'a
c
' | sort)

sections.title: Text Processing
sections.description: Cut, search and transform text with core utilities.

snippets.code:
# Pick columns and rows
printf 'ada:36:london\ngrace:40:new york\n' | cut -d: -f1,3
printf 'ada:36\ngrace:40\n' | awk -F: '$2 > 37 { print $1 }'

# Search and replace with sed
printf 'red green red\n' | sed 's/red/blue/g'

# Count repeated values
printf 'b\na\nb\n' | sort | uniq -c

# Grep with line numbers and fixed strings
grep -n -F "root" /etc/passwd
grep -c "^#" /etc/services      # count comment lines

# Translate characters and squeeze repeats
printf 'Hello   World\n' | tr -s ' ' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'

# Show the first and last line
printf '1\n2\n3\n4\n' | sed -n '1p;$p'

# Sum a numeric column with awk
printf '10 apples
5 pears
7 plums
' | awk '{ total += $1 } END { print total }'

# Extract every IP address from a log
printf '10.0.0.5 - ok
192.168.1.7 - fail
' | grep -oE '([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}'

sections.title: Files and Directories
sections.description: Create, locate and clean up files and directories.

snippets.code:
# Create and inspect
mkdir -p notes/2026
touch notes/2026/todo.txt
ls -lh notes/2026
stat -c '%n %s bytes %y' notes/2026/todo.txt

# Copy, move and remove
cp notes/2026/todo.txt notes/todo.bak
mv notes/todo.bak notes/2026/old.txt
rm notes/2026/old.txt

# Find files by name, type and age
find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.txt'
find /var/log -type f -mtime -7 -name '*.log'
find . -type d -empty

# Act on each result and show what is removed
find . -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.bak' -print -delete

# Read a file line by line, preserving whitespace
while IFS= read -r line; do
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
done < /etc/hostname

# Compare two files and show the difference
diff -u notes/2026/todo.txt notes/2026/old.txt

sections.title: Permissions
sections.description: Read and change modes, ownership and special bits.

snippets.code:
# Symbolic and numeric modes
chmod +x deploy.sh          # add execute for everyone
chmod 644 notes.txt         # rw-r--r--
chmod 755 scripts           # rwxr-xr-x
chmod u+w,g-w report.txt

# Recursive change that touches only existing directories
chmod -R u+rwX shared

# Ownership changes need root for files you do not own
chown ada:developers project.txt
chgrp developers project.txt

# Read the mode, owner and group
stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' project.txt

# setuid, setgid and sticky bits
chmod 4755 backup-tool
chmod 2775 shared-dir
chmod 1777 /tmp

sections.title: Jobs and Processes
sections.description: List processes, send signals and manage jobs.

snippets.code:
# List and search running processes
ps aux | grep -F sshd
pgrep -a sshd
top -b -n 1 | head -n 15

# Send signals
kill -TERM 4242      # polite shutdown
kill -9 4242         # force (last resort)
pkill -f "python3 server.py"

# Background jobs in the current shell
sleep 30 &
job=$!
echo "started job $job"
jobs -l
wait "$job"
echo "finished with status $?"

# Keep a job alive after the terminal closes
nohup ./backup.sh > backup.log 2>&1 &

sections.title: Environment and Startup
sections.description: Inspect exported variables and startup files.

snippets.code:
# Show the environment
printenv | sort | head -n 20
echo "$PATH"
env | grep -E '^(HOME|SHELL|USER)='

# Export a variable to child processes
export EDITOR=vim
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Temporary environment for a single command
LANG=C date +%A

# Login shells read ~/.bash_profile or ~/.profile
# Interactive non-login shells read ~/.bashrc
# Put aliases and prompt settings in ~/.bashrc

# Reload the current shell configuration
source ~/.bashrc
. ~/.bashrc

# Check whether this is a login shell
shopt -q login_shell && echo "login shell" || echo "not a login shell"

sections.title: Script Safety
sections.description: Fail fast, quote expansions and clean up on exit.

snippets.code:
# Refuse to run as root and work from a known directory
if (( EUID == 0 )); then
  echo "do not run this as root" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1

# Quote every expansion and use -- to end options
rm -f -- "./cache.tmp"
printf '%s\n' "$HOME"

# Remove temporary files even when the script fails
workdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$workdir"' EXIT
printf 'data\n' > "$workdir/input.txt"

# Catch errors and report the line
trap 'echo "failed at line $LINENO" >&2' ERR
set -E

sections.title: Debugging
sections.description: Trace execution and find the line that broke.

snippets.code:
# Print each command before running it
set -x
name="Ada"
echo "Hello, $name"
set +x

# Verbose shell input
bash -v script.sh

# Syntax check without executing anything
bash -n script.sh

# Add file and line number to the trace
PS4='+ ${BASH_SOURCE}:${LINENO}: '
set -x
for i in 1 2; do echo "i=$i"; done
set +x

# Stop at the first error and report where it happened
set -eE
trap 'echo "failed at line $LINENO" >&2' ERR
false

sections.title: Common Recipes
sections.description: Ready-made scripts for routine tasks.

snippets.code:
# Timestamped backup of a directory
src="$HOME/Documents"
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
dest="$HOME/backups/documents-$stamp.tar.gz"

mkdir -p "$HOME/backups"
tar -czf "$dest" -C "$HOME" Documents
echo "wrote $dest"

# Retry a command up to three times
retry() {
  local tries=3
  local n=1

  until "$@"; do
    if (( n >= tries )); then
      echo "gave up after $tries attempts" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    echo "attempt $n failed, retrying" >&2
    ((n++))
    sleep 2
  done
}

retry curl -fsS https://example.com/health

# Ten largest files under the home directory
du -ah "$HOME" 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -n 10

# Remove files older than 30 days from a cache directory
find "$HOME/.cache/builds" -type f -mtime +30 -print -delete
